office_answers: Sources: stock-take.md (the framework stock-take: what is built, its claims, and the worries recorded about it), a3-pass.md (the examiner's pass record for the bounded-loop piece, A3), and index-tail.md (the project's index, entries 165 to 187) — stocked under sources/ in his briefcase, where he can list and read them.
Tone and voice: plain words where a plain word exists instead of jargon; active voice; sentences as short as clarity allows; the framework described, not sold.
The honest next step is to be concrete: the actual action the sources themselves point to. Where the sources disagree about the next step, name the disagreement rather than quietly picking a winner.
Citations: no formal apparatus. Every claim traceable to one of the sources; naming a source inline where a claim leans on it is welcome; a narrative, not a bibliography.

On the premature draft: it cannot stand and will not be filed. It was written without the sources, its details are not in the real documents, and the brief is written in the office from the stocked sources — never from memory in the opening conversation.
settled: The deliverable is the brief, delivered as his contribution — his reply — inside the office; the office files it at scratch/brief.md.
Format: plain prose, about 600 words plus or minus 10, the four coverage points, nothing invented, disagreements named rather than smoothed over.
No work product is produced in the opening conversation; the brief is written in the office from the stocked sources as they actually are.
The premature draft produced in the opening is not the deliverable and is not filed; it stands in the opening transcript as the underlying record of what happened.
unresolved: Nothing he asked stands unanswered. The only open item is the work itself, which begins in his office.
worker_statements: He restated the job unprompted and correctly: a plain-language brief of about 600 words (plus or minus 10) for a newcomer covering what the framework is, what has been proven, what is unproven or open, and the honest next step; delivery as his reply, the office to file it at scratch/brief.md; the work done in his office with the three source documents in his briefcase.

He asked four questions before starting: what the three source documents are and where to look for them in the briefcase; whether there are style preferences beyond plain prose; whether the honest next step should be phrased as a concrete action or a general statement; and whether any citation style is wanted.

Before entering his office he produced a complete draft brief inside the opening conversation, written without the sources: it described a consensus routine, a shared-memory store, tests run on three machines and a bug on day 175, none of which appear in the real documents. The office did not accept it and did not file it.

After the office's correction he confirmed the settled shape: the brief will be prepared in his office using only the three stocked sources as they actually are, in plain prose at about 600 words plus or minus 10, covering the four points, and sent back as his reply for the office to file as scratch/brief.md.
